samples.summary: afterEach cleanup is unguarded: a throw from `editor.dispose()` (or `removeChild`) skips every restore below it, including the new `navigator.platform` teardown
samples.evidence: The delta's stated goal is "drop the stub instead of leaving a Mac platform on the navigator for whatever runs next" (lines 116-119), but that code sits at the END of an unprotected sequence starting at line 107 `editor.dispose();` / line 108 `document.body.removeChild(container);`. If either throws — e.g. a test leaves the editor in a state where dispose rethrows, or `container` was already detached — none of lines 109-120 run, so `HTMLCanvasElement.prototype.getContext`, `requestAnimationFrame`, `ResizeObserver`, `OffscreenCanvas` and the `MacIntel` platform stub all leak into subsequent files sharing the jsdom environment, which is exactly the failure mode this hunk was written to prevent. Wrapping the global restores in try/finally (or ordering them before dispose) closes the gap.

samples.summary: Sibling global restores assign `undefined` rather than deleting, leaving own properties that never existed in plain jsdom
samples.evidence: Lines 111-112 restore `globalThis.ResizeObserver` / `globalThis.OffscreenCanvas` by assigning the captured value, which is `undefined` under plain jsdom (neither exists there). That creates own properties whose value is `undefined` instead of removing them — the same asymmetry the new `platform` branch (lines 115-120) was added to fix. Harmless for the current consumers (`canvas-measurer.ts:87-91` and `editor.ts:2594` use truthiness/direct construction), so no behavioral bug today, but an `in`-style probe elsewhere would observe the difference.

mergedFrom.summary: Cmd+Backspace can still delete every earlier visual line when affinity is 'forward' (e.g. immediately after Home)
getWrapAffinity uses the body layout and cannot see cell blocks, so post-typing affinity is 'backward' in headers/footers/table cells — which now changes Home/End
moveVertical still calls findVisualLine with the 'forward' default, now inconsistent with the affinity-aware helpers
End can now move the caret backwards at a wrap boundary with trailing spaces

finding.summary: Table-cell hit-testing never produces 'forward' affinity, so Home/End inside a cell now act on the previous visual line
finding.evidence: getVisualLineRange's table-cell branch (text-editor.ts:4029) now honours `lineAffinity`, defaulting to `this.cursor.lineAffinity`. But every cell cursor-placement path hard-codes 'backward': single click `this.cursor.moveTo(cellPos)` (1584, no affinity arg → Cursor.moveTo default 'backward', cursor.ts:28), double/triple/shift-click (1552/1562/1573), and resolveHFCellOffset returns `lineAffinity: 'backward'` unconditionally (4509, 4515). resolveOffsetInCellAtXY (4630) does not even return an affinity field. Consequence: click at the START of a soft-wrapped visual line inside a table cell yields offset == the wrap boundary with affinity 'backward'; getVisualLineRange now resolves that to the PREVIOUS visual line, so Home moves the caret up to the previous line's start and End moves it back to the previous line's end — before this change both correctly acted on the clicked line. The body path is safe only because findPositionAtPixel's affinityForOffset (find-position-at-pixel.ts:116) returns 'forward' there; the cell path has no equivalent.

verdict.reason: All cited code is present as described. getVisualLineRange's table-cell branch honours lineAffinity (text-editor.ts:4029-4031) defaulting to this.cursor.lineAffinity (4001), yet no cell cursor-placement path can ever yield 'forward': single click uses cursor.moveTo(cellPos) with no affinity (1584), double/triple/shift click likewise (1552/1562/1573), in-cell arrow movement likewise (2736), Cursor.moveTo defaults to 'backward' (cursor.ts:28-30), resolveHFCellOffset hard-codes 'backward' (4509/4515), and resolveOffsetInCellAtXY returns no affinity at all (4630-4635) while computing an offset equal to the wrap boundary for a click at a wrapped line's start (4745-4751). The body path has the missing counterpart (find-position-at-pixel.ts:116-117, consumed at text-editor.ts:1615/1618). Consequence: Home (2786) and End (2799) inside a table cell resolve to the previous visual line at any soft-wrap boundary. Cell caret rendering shares the same backward rule (peer-cursor.ts:196-206), which makes the behavior self-consistent but does not show it is correct; no guard or unreachability argument refutes the finding, so it stands as a real boundary/affinity logic bug in the correctness lane.
